basic_identification.full_title: Bulk Handling Equipment — Wagon Marshalling Equipment — Endless Rope Type — General Requirements (राशि प्रहस्तन उपस्कर — रेल डिब्बा (वैगन) विन्यास उपस्कर — सिरा विहीन रस्सानुमा टाइप — सामान्य अपेक्षाएँ)
basic_identification.sector_category: Heavy Mechanical Engineering / Bulk Handling Equipment (approved by the Heavy Mechanical Engineering Division Council and finalized by the Bulk Handling Equipment Sectional Committee, HMD 07, of the Bureau of Indian Standards)

scope.summary: This Indian Standard prescribes the general construction, material, safety, control, performance, and testing requirements for transportable or fixed endless or open rope type wagon marshalling equipment used for the vertical, horizontal, or side-hitching transport of railway wagons on tracks during bulk loading and unloading operations.

certification_and_marking.standard_type: Product Specification / System Design and Performance Code (Heavy Mechanical Engineering Department / Bulk Material Handling)
certification_and_marking.certification_status: Voluntary Certification under the Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS). However, compliance with IS 13065 is highly critical and routinely mandated in public sector mining (Coal India, SCCL), thermal power plants (NTPC), port authorities, steel mills, and railway sidings across India to prevent derailments or high-tension cable snaps.

requirements.detail: Any numerical value representing the result of a physical dimension, ratio, or calculated pressure must be mathematically rounded off in accordance with IS 2:1960. The number of significant places retained should match that of the specified value in the standard.

The structural base frame carrying the haulage winch, motor, and gearboxes must be fabricated from hot-rolled steel sections conforming to IS 808, machined flat on mating surfaces, heavily gusseted at corners, and securely bolted in sections to facilitate transport and handling.

To prevent premature wire fatigue, the ratio of the rope drum tread diameter (D) to the nominal wire rope diameter (d) must conform to strict minimum limits based on rope construction: (a) Round strand 6x7 construction = 42, (b) Round strand 6x19 construction = 24, (c) Round strand 6x37 construction = 19.
The pitch and diameter of rope drum grooves must be machined strictly in accordance with IS 3937 : 1967 to ensure smooth cable spooling.

The radial pressure (P, in MPa) exerted by the tensioned wire rope on the drum or sheave is calculated using the formula: P = (20 * T) / (D * d), where T is rope tension in kg, D is drum tread diameter in mm, and d is rope diameter in mm.

The calculated radial pressure (P) must not exceed standard limits: (a) for 6x7 ropes: 2.1 MPa (Cast Iron) or 3.85 MPa (Cast Steel); (b) for 6x19 ropes: 3.5 MPa (Cast Iron) or 6.30 MPa (Cast Steel); (c) for 6x37 ropes: 4.2 MPa (Cast Iron) or 7.50 MPa (Cast Steel).
If agreed between the manufacturer and buyer, the rope drum shell can be fitted with renewable segments of chilled cast iron surge pads to simplify maintenance and protect the core drum.

An automatic, remote-controlled thruster-operated brake acting directly on the wheel or shaft is required for service and emergency braking. The brake assembly must be fitted with dedicated switches to indicate 'On', 'Off', and 'Wear' positions.

Reduction is achieved in two stages (enclosed gearbox running in an oil bath, plus open spur gear reduction with guards). For drives up to 30 kW, a worm reduction gearbox is permitted; above 30 kW, helical or spiral bevel-helical reduction gearboxes are preferred.

The reduction gearbox must be rated in accordance with IS 7403, using minimum service factors based on daily duty hours: 1.1 for up to 8 hours/day, 1.25 for up to 12 hours/day, and 1.50 for continuous 24-hour daily service.

Winch assemblies must utilize flexible couplings between the motor and gearbox. For high-capacity drives exceeding 40 kW, fluid couplings must be integrated to absorb high starting torque shocks and prevent rope snapping.
Winch drum shafts must be supported by split gun metal bearings, phosphor bronze bushes, or self-aligning spherical roller bearings mounted in cast iron plummer blocks with grease nipples.
To maintain a constant snubbing tension on the friction drive winch in both directions, the system must incorporate an automatic, counter-weighted gravity take-up device.

Track and vertical guide rollers must be dual-flanged at both ends, featuring parallel barrels fitted with sealed, grease-filled, single-row deep groove ball bearings designed to withstand dust, water, and debris on railway siding floors.

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 13065 : 1991 (Reaffirmed 2022) is the national Indian Standard prescribing the general technical, material, design, and performance requirements for endless or open rope type wagon marshalling equipment. Developed under the Bulk Handling Equipment Sectional Committee (HMD 07), the standard regulates traction systems used to haul railway wagons on tracks during bulk loading and unloading. It enforces precise drum-to-rope sizing ratios based on rope construction, defines a strict radial pressure formula to limit groove corrugation, mandates automatic thruster-operated brakes with wear indicators, requires helical gearboxes for motor power above 30 kW, enforces fluid couplings above 40 kW, and specifies automatic gravity take-up units to maintain uniform traction tension in both directions, ensuring rugged, high-safety operations in mines, power plants, and industrial siding yards.
